title: Security & Deployment Review - Zenith Payments
topics: Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private tradeoffs
next_steps: Redwood to send SOC 2 Type II report and security whitepaper
Customer to share current KMS architecture and retention policy
Schedule a short pilot run (1-week) on Dedicated cluster for payments workload
Pricing/commit estimate for a dedicated 8-GPU pool
action_items: Maya Chen | Send SOC2 Type II report + security whitepaper + link to privacy page | 2025-12-05
Devon Patel | Share KMS rotation policy, key hierarchy diagram (redacted) | 2025-12-07
Luca Ortega | Produce rough latency/cost estimate using Zenith sample traces | 2025-12-10
Marcus Li | Provide sample SAML IdP metadata and RBAC roles matrix | 2025-12-06
header:
Date: 2025-12-03 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~55 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Luca Ortega (Redwood SE), Rachel Kim (Zenith - Head of Platform), Devon Patel (Zenith - Security Lead), Marcus Li (Zenith - Infra), Olivia Carter (Zenith - Procurement)
summary: Security posture deep-dive for Zenith Payments evaluating Redwood hosted vs dedicated vs private. Primary concerns: SOC2/ISO evidence, SSO and RBAC integration, KMS/encryption at rest, audit logs/retention, and data deletion policies. Redwood AE/SE provided high-level architecture options and agreed to share compliance artifacts and run a short dedicated pilot for workload validation.
transcript:
[00:00] Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Uh this is Maya from Redwood, I'm the AE on the account, with Luca, our solutions engineer.
[00:10] Luca: Hi all, Luca here. We'll dive into security and deployment options.
[00:20] Rachel: Thanks — appreciate it. Quick context: we're evaluating for payment fraud detection and a few settlement microservices, so PCI-similar constraints, though we're not looking to store card numbers in Redwood obviously.
[00:35] Devon: The big checklist for us is SOC2 or ISO evidence, SSO integration via SAML, RBAC controls, audit logging retention, and encryption keys — we use a customer-managed KMS already.
[00:50] Maya: Great, that's what we expected. Quick question on timeline — are you aiming for a pilot before EOY or Q1?
[00:55] Rachel: Targeting Q1 but we'd like a short pilot in December if possible, to validate latency.
[01:05] Luca: Okay. Architecturally, Redwood offers Hosted (fastest), Dedicated (reserved GPU pool), and Private (VPC/on-prem). For payments, many customers use Dedicated with VPC peering or Private for strict data residency.
[01:20] Marcus: When you say "Private" — do you mean on-prem or VPC only? We need the option for air-gapped in the future.
[01:28] Luca: Both are options. Private can be deployed inside your VPC or packaged for air-gapped environments. There's some lead time for air-gapped installs, typically a few weeks for planning and approval.
[01:40] Devon: Let's talk SOC 2. Do you have Type II? We're going to need that and ideally evidence of the scope covering log retention and access controls.
[01:50] Maya: Yes, we have SOC 2 Type II for the platform. We'll send the redacted report — it covers the hosted control plane and our dedicated offerings.
[02:00] Olivia: And ISO? We're ISO-aligned for some vendors — is Redwood ISO 27001 certified?
[02:06] Luca: We are in progress on ISO 27001. We're able to provide compensating controls and our risk assessments today; ISO cert targeted next quarter.
[02:15] Rachel: That's fine as long as the SOC 2 and our internal risk team can sign off — we'll run the paperwork.
[02:22] Devon: On SSO, we run Okta with SAML. We need SCIM provisioning and enforcement of RBAC so engineers can't see production transcript data.
[02:32] Maya: Supported — we integrate SAML SSO and SCIM for user provisioning. RBAC is configurable per org and per project; you can map SAML groups to roles.
[02:42] Marcus: Any gotchas with session length or token expiry? We have strict session limits.
[02:48] Luca: Session settings are configurable; if you use our hosted option we enforce refresh token policies and idle timeouts. For Private, you control token lifetimes via your IdP.
[02:58] Rachel: Audit logs: we need immutable audit trails of who requested what prompt, IP addresses, timestamps, and model version. Retention policy ideally 1 year.
[03:08] Luca: Redwood audit logs capture request metadata and can be exported to your SIEM. Default retention on Hosted is 90 days, but Dedicated and Private customers can configure longer retention or forward to S3/Graylog/Splunk for long-term storage.
[03:22] Devon: Are logs tamper-evident or append-only? We need to show integrity for forensics.
[03:28] Maya: We support WORM-style exports and can provide guidance on write-once storage. For production telemetry we also publish log hashes on request so you can verify integrity.
[03:38] Olivia: Encryption at rest — we have a corporate KMS (AWS KMS); we'd prefer customer-managed keys.
[03:44] Luca: Customer-managed keys are supported for Dedicated and Private. Hosted supports BYOK integrations via KMS for certain plans; there are nuances for multi-tenant hosted environments. We'll send specifics.
[03:55] Marcus: How about key rotation and access policies? We rotate keys every 90 days internally.
[04:00] Luca: Our integrations work with key rotation; you can schedule rotation in KMS and Redwood will handle rewraps when we detect rotation. Access to KMS is limited to the control plane and uses least-privilege service principals.
[04:10] Rachel: Data residency — we need data for EU users to stay in eu-central region. Is that possible with dedicated?
[04:17] Maya: Yes, you can pin regions for Dedicated clusters. Private can be entirely inside your VPC in eu-central. Hosted also has regional endpoints but check the data plane locality depending on plan.
[04:30] Devon: Can you speak to model artifact retention? If a model checkpoint is uploaded, what's the retention and who controls deletion?
[04:36] Luca: Models and artifacts are tied to account storage. You can set deletion policies, and we support programmatic deletion via API. For Private, you control storage lifecycle fully.
[04:48] Rachel: PCI-specific question — you mentioned not storing card data. Our flows tokenize card data upstream; does Redwood see tokens? That might still be considered cardholder data if reversible.
[05:00] Maya: Important point. We recommend token redaction prior to sending. We also have a policy and tooling for PII scrubbing; for payments workload many customers run a pre-processing step to strip or hash tokens.
[05:12] Devon: Ok. About penetration testing — do you allow customer-led pentests or third-party assessments against the Dedicated deployment?
[05:20] Luca: We do allow pentests with coordinated disclosure for Dedicated and Private. For Hosted, we require a small compliance process and a time-window. We'll share the pentest policy doc.
[05:30] Olivia: Procurement asks — will we need an addendum for data processing and DPA?
[05:36] Maya: Yes, we have a DPA template and a data processing addendum for enterprise customers; we'll share it with legal.
[05:42] Rachel: On the security operations side, do you provide SOC alerts or do we rely on forwarded logs?
[05:48] Luca: We stream logs; we also have an optional managed security add-on for managed alerts and 24/7 monitoring. For Dedicated customers there's an ops channel for faster escalation.
[06:00] [small cross-talk]
[06:05] Devon: One more — can you guarantee that private chats/prompts are not used for model training?
[06:12] Maya: We have an explicit no-training promise for enterprise customers — we can put that in the contract. Hosted public-tier models may have different terms, but Dedicated/Private includes contractual commitments about no training on your data.
[06:24] Marcus: For the pilot, we're going to run a sample workload — around 500 request/s peak, average prompt length ~800 tokens, inference windows small. Any red flags?
[06:36] Luca: Roughly speaking, that lines up with a medium-sized dedicated pool. We'll run sims once you share traces; latency SLOs depend on model size and quantization.
[06:45] Rachel: Are there any compliance gaps we should flag to our risk team?
[06:50] Luca: Today ISO is in-progress; otherwise SOC2 Type II is available. For PCI scope you'll need to document tokens and the end-to-end flow. We can provide architecture diagrams and a responsibilities matrix (who controls what).
[07:03] Devon: On RBAC specifics: can I limit users so only certain roles can call production models and see logs, while others can only call a sandbox model?
[07:12] Maya: Yep — role-based policies let you lock down models, deployment routes, and audit log access. You can also restrict API keys per environment.
[07:22] Rachel: What about network controls — can we enforce IP allowlists and private peering?
[07:28] Luca: Dedicated supports VPC peering, private endpoints, and IP allowlists. We also support mutual TLS for private peering.
[07:38] Olivia: For SAML groups mapping — do we get a default roles matrix or do you expect us to define from scratch?
[07:44] Maya: We provide templates and a recommended roles matrix for payments customers; we can pre-populate and you can adjust.
[07:52] [pause — everyone reviewing notes]
[08:00] Marcus: Anything about cost impacts — e.g., if we enable long retention for logs, what's typical?
[08:06] Luca: Exporting to your S3 is cost-effective; we charge for ingest and optional storage when we host logs. If you keep logs in your S3, Redwood's cost is minimal. We'll include an example cost table.
[08:20] Devon: How does rollover/fallback work if a Dedicated pool hits capacity? Do you fail open to hosted? That's a risk for us.
[08:28] Luca: You control routing policies. Default for enterprise is to fail closed — we won't route to hosted unless you opt in. We can set canary or fallback policies per route.
[08:38] Rachel: Good. Any notes on backups and disaster recovery?
[08:42] Maya: Dedicated clusters have snapshot-based backups and cross-zone replication. Private DR depends on deployment; we can provide options.
[08:52] Devon: Ok, let's talk about artifacts you will send.
[08:55] Maya: We'll send: SOC2 Type II report (redacted), security whitepaper, pentest policy, DPA, private deployment checklist, and KMS integration notes. Also a short RBAC template.
[09:10] Olivia: From procurement, we'll need cost/commit for a dedicated 8-GPU pool and the pilot terms.
[09:17] Maya: Understood. Luca will prepare an estimate and a pilot scope doc.
[09:24] [background typing noises]
[09:30] Rachel: Minor transcription note — some of our team may be busy next week; can we get the docs asap so we can pre-review?
[09:36] Maya: Yes, we'll send by Friday.
[09:40] Devon: One last technical detail — KV cache and model version pinning. We need deterministic inference for certain rules.
[09:48] Luca: You can pin model versions and disable automatic updates. KV cache behavior is configurable; for deterministic runs we suggest fixed seeds and pinned weights. We'll document recommended settings.
[09:59] Maya: Alright, sounds like we're aligned. Quick recap and next steps?
[10:04] Rachel: Go ahead.
[10:06] Maya: Action items: I'll send SOC2 + whitepaper + DPA; Luca will send pilot estimate and latency/cost sims; Devon will share KMS key rotation policy; Marcus will share SAML metadata. We'll target the pilot in mid-December.
[10:20] Devon: Agreed, I'll loop in our risk team after we get SOC2.
[10:25] Olivia: I'll wait for procurement terms.
[10:28] Maya: Thanks everyone. We'll follow up in email with links to the docs and a proposed pilot schedule.
[10:32] Rachel: Thanks, bye.
[10:35] [call ends — total duration ~55 minutes]
notes: Customer emphasized need for no-training contractual clause for enterprise data.
Redwood to avoid automatic failover to hosted unless customer opts in — important procurement point.
Customer prefers KMS BYOK for Dedicated; hosted BYOK details needed.
